items.content_html:
FF148 adds support for addHandler() method of NavigationPrecommitController in https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2009004.

This allows you to add a post commit handler in your precommit handler, rather than statically passing it in the object when intercept() is called. You'll use this if the precommit affects the post commit.

This adds docs for the method.

Still to do

  • Add exmample to addHandler() showing how is used.
  • update NavigateEvent/.intercept() - this has lots of workflow. That is a bit changed by the existence of addHandler
  • may update Navigation_API - at least review

Related work tracked in #42780
items.title: FF148 NavigationPrecommitController.addHandler() docs

items.content_html:
FF148 Supports using Document.execCommand with option "paste" in web content in https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1998195#c18

Previously this would only work on extensions. The change in FF is a reimplementation of the feature using the Clipboard API. So basically you can now paste in web content as well. Transient activation is required. same origin content can paste without anything else, but for cross origin content you get a paste-prompt UI that you have to use to grant the permission.

With a readClipboard permission an extension can read cross-origin content without the prompt or transient activation. This is as documented in https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Clipboard_API#security_considerations.

Safari seems to use the same model as FF and testing using the example I added here shows support is at least similarl.

Anyway, this updates the paste option to note that this is supported in content, and how, and point to browser compat. There is also an example that eases testing.

Related docs work can be tracked in #42747
items.title: FF148 Document.execCommand() with paste option - FF/Safari updates

Description

I decided to update the Basic HTML syntax learning area article to improve the wording and make it more friendly to beginners, for example:

  • Making some of the examples a bit simpler, and others a bit more explanatory.
  • Removing some content that isn't helpful to beginners. For example, mentioning valid XML when talking about closing slashes, and including a discussion on the innerHTML JavaScript property when talking about whitespace. These are way out of scope for the current article and will just confuse beginners. MDN prides itself on its completeness, but a different approach is needed for the Learn area.
  • Cutting down on verbiage and simplifying explanations.
  • Using modern live sample syntax, which in a couple of cases was used to fix broken rendering.

Motivation

Additional details

Related issues and pull requests

items.content_html:
Description

This pull request clarifies that Array.prototype.map() does not mutate the original array and instead returns a new array.

Motivation

This clarification helps avoid confusion for readers who may assume that map() modifies the existing array, especially beginners learning JavaScript array methods.

Additional details

No functional changes were made. This is a documentation-only improvement.

Related issues and pull requests
items.title: docs: clarify that Array.map does not mutate the original array
